title: Senior Counsel
description:
About Us
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Overview:

Visa is seeking a proactive product and commercial lawyer to join as Senior Counsel as part of the legal team supporting Visa’s Risk and Security Intelligence Solutions (RAS) organization. The position will report to a Senior Managing Counsel on the Value-Added Services Legal Team.

The primary responsibility of the role is to provide legal support for key RAS growth initiatives, product development, commercial transactions, acquisitions, and integration activities across a broad portfolio of fraud, risk, identity, and authentication solutions. The attorney will serve as a strategic legal partner to the RAS organization on a wide range of matters, with responsibilities spanning existing product lines and new business development.

A near-term priority will include supporting Visa’s proposed acquisition of BioCatch, a leading provider of behavioral biometrics and advanced fraud detection. The proposed transaction is subject to regulatory approval. Pre-close, the role will focus on Visa-side integration planning, regulatory coordination, and legal preparedness efforts. Post-close, the candidate will support integration execution and provide ongoing legal counsel for the acquired business.

The attorney will work closely with other experienced Visa lawyers and compliance professionals and regularly engage directly with business clients, including as a trusted advisor to BioCatch and RAS leadership.

Applicants must be skilled at managing multiple priorities and multiple time zones in a fast-paced and challenging, but highly rewarding, environment; have good judgment and strong analytical, client counseling, and negotiation skills; be an adept issuer spotter and creative problem solver; be self-motivated; and, most importantly, be an optimistic, curious, and collaborative leader and team player.

The role is based in Atlanta, GA. Candidates who currently sit in a Visa office in the U.S. are eligible to apply.

  • Ensure compliance with pre-closing obligations and information-sharing protocols
  • Work closely with business and cross-functional teams to understand and achieve key business objectives and help them develop compelling product and service offerings
  • Provide advice and counsel to business line and management on transactional legal matters, proposed corporate actions, and product launches
  • Draft, negotiate, and drive to completion complex commercial agreements that achieve business objectives, and continue to support those business relationships once consummated
  • Provide sophisticated and creative counseling and advice to business teams regarding product development, deployment, and associated commercial and contracting considerations
  • Manage regulatory support, including monitoring conditions or commitments arising from the regulatory approval process, jurisdiction-specific regulatory assessments, and evaluation of how shifts in regulatory landscapes may impact Visa and its partners
  • Work closely with Visa’s regional legal and business teams globally, and assist these teams in resolving regional and local issues, including to achieve consistency on approaches and issues by Visa worldwide
  • Review externally facing documentation for compliance with securities laws, disclosure policies, data use policies and requirements, competition law issues, etc.
  • Where required, coordinate and supervise outside counsel for timeliness, cost-effectiveness, and excellence of service and work product

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or at least 8 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters/ MBA/JD/MD) or at least 3 years of work experience with a PhD

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 12 or more years of work experience with a bachelor’s degree or 8-10 years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or 6+ years of work experience with a PhD.
  • Strong academic credentials, including a J.D. degree (or international equivalent)
  • Valid license to practice in the state where the job is located or the ability to become state registered in-house counsel in good standing
  • Prior experience in at least one of the following areas: payments (and related credit and debit processing), financial services, technology or fintech industries experience
  • Prior experience in complex global, cross-jurisdictional projects, including transactions subject to antitrust or regulatory review.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive execution in a team environment, integrating legal advice and business knowledge while providing balanced advice regarding risks and benefits
  • Must be able to work independently and collaboratively as needed, and engage directly with business clients at all levels
  • Must be a practical and creative problem-solver with developed business acumen and the ability to understand the company's business interests and anticipate the nature and magnitude of issues that could arise in various settings
  • Must be able to manage and drive the legal and regulatory aspects of complex business initiatives, both in the U.S. and internationally
  • Transactional background (corporate, commercial arrangements) with extensive experience drafting and negotiating a wide array of commercial agreements
  • Working knowledge of privacy and competition laws
  • Must be able to multitask and manage a significant workload and many clients with minimal supervision, while providing timely responses to inquiries.

title: Pediatric Education Program Manager
description:
Site: The General Hospital Corporation


Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.


Job Summary

This position provides management and administrative support for the efficient and effective administration of the Pediatric Education Programs under the direction of the Pediatric Vice Chair of Education, the Mass General Brigham for Children (MGBfC) Administrative Director, and the Residency and Fellowship Program Directors. The focus of this position centers on managing the team of coordinators and maintaining the educational quality of our ACGME accredited training programs along with managing required accreditation components of those programs with and for Program Directors as well as the Undergraduate Medical Program.

-Serves as central resource for educational activities within MGBfC.
-Continually assesses and manages a wide range of programmatic issues, including curricula development, long-range planning, project development, departmental initiatives, and ongoing educational activities.
-Makes recommendations for improving educational curricula, meeting ACGME requirements, and streamlining or sharing resources for more efficient processes across the educational programs.
-Recommends policy development and/or maintenance of policies in accordance with institutional Graduate Medical Education, Harvard Medical School, and Committee of Interns and Residents union policies.
-Coordinates overarching department-wide educational events and initiatives as directed by the Vice Chair of Education.
-Coordinates overarching events and meetings to include the annual Medical Education Summit, annual Pediatric Fellows Retreat, alumni association, etc.
-Prepares meeting agendas, materials, and submits resulting reports to GME and ACGME for required biannual Clinical Competency Committees (CCCs), bi-annual Scholarly Oversight Committees, and annual Program Education Committees (PECs) for multiple fellowships.
-Tracks national and hospital deadlines and projects to ensure on-time completion.
-Manages regularly occurring team meeting agendas with Program Directors and coordinators for assignment of tasks; works in conjunction with coordinators to complete tasks.
-Trains new coordinators on basic functions and systems such as recruitment processes, ERAS, NRMP etc.; serves as short-term backup during turnover and/or leaves.
-Ensures processes and deadlines are met for recruitment and onboarding.
-Assists the Fellowship Program Directors with individual Fellow compliance to academic requirements and hospital regulations, record and report completion, and confidential disciplinary actions.
-Provides input and oversight into developing education budget and monitoring/maintenance of such.
-Independently manages special projects assigned by the Pediatric Vice Chair of Education, Program Directors, and MGBfC Administrative Director.

This position also provides general administrative management support for educational programs in the Department specifically as it relates to trainee evaluation, including functioning as a specialist for New Innovations, monitoring and tracking ACGME, ABP, and ABIM policies to identify compliance issues, tracking of resident work hours and general trainee file maintenance, compilation and reporting of program data and oversight of future alumni projects. The position provides budget oversight for the programs and is a resource for the education administrative staff supporting the education programs under the various physician program directors.

Excellent interpersonal, communication and organizational skills are required.


Qualifications

Education Program Responsibilities

  • Monitors, interprets and communicates ACGME, ABP, ABIM, and hospital policies to support compliance.
  • Completes required national and hospital surveys or reports, including the annual ACGME ADS submission and MGB GME APE submissions for all department-sponsored clinical Pediatric fellowships.
  • Uses web-based programs such as ACGME WebADS, ERAS, NRMP, and others for surveys, scheduling, and reports.
  • Coordinates overarching department-wide educational events and initiatives as directed by the Pediatric Vice Chair of Education, such as the annual Pediatric Medical Education Summit.
  • Functions as the New Innovation expert providing general training and uploads initial data for incoming trainees to GME/New Innovations from ERAS.
  • Creates annual schedules and evaluative sessions in New Innovations across multiple fellowships; ensures timely completion of trainee, faculty, and program evaluations.
  • Monitors duty hours periodically and ensures trainee completion of education-related hospital and national required surveys.
  • Monitors faculty evaluation completion during the academic year to ensure the overarching 80% institutional benchmark is met by the end of the academic year across multiple programs.
  • Assists in the development of competency-based initiatives, maintains tracking of competency assessment and coordinates feedback on continuous quality improvements of fellowship programs.
  • Develops and maintains fellows’ electronic confidential personnel files with required documentation and records, e.g. ERAS application, USMLE, ECFMG report, etc.), evaluation summary reports, milestone reports, ILPs, QI project summaries, annual contracts, ABP or other required documents, procedure and case logs if required, documentation of program director semi-annual performance reviews of fellows, scholarly oversight data, and graduation, dismissal, or transfer documents.
  • Reports to hospital offices with trainee data for required systems/audits.
  • Supports future alumni outreach project.
  • Assist Program Directors in establishing policies and procedures and implementing Departmental policies and procedures within the Program. Evaluates, initiates, and implements various systems and procedures and revises them as necessary to maximize efficiency.
  • Support education leadership meetings.
  • Work with the VP/Administrative Director to develop annual operating and capital budgets for education programs.
  • Monitor all program finances including reconciliation of monthly fund statements, tracking of all HMS expenses, invoice generation for HMS, coordination with Accounts Payable, Research Finance, Payroll, and other departments as needed for resolution of errors or identification of charges, approval of requisitions through eBuy, development and maintenance of a fiscal record keeping system.
  • Oversee affiliation agreements with outside organizations to ensure contract completion and collections.
  • Acts as an administrative resource for education administrative support staff and under program physician director and administrative director oversight facilitates recruitment, interviewing, hiring, training, and disciplining of all service personnel.
  • Informs staff of Hospital and Division and Departmental policies and procedures.
  • Manage weekly payroll through UKG for education program staff according to HR policies and maintains payroll-related records. Coordinates with Human Resources, MGPO Office, Administrative Director, Payroll, and Research Finance Offices for processing of all employee changes in Workday.
  • Serve as representative of the MGBfC and Hospital as requested for committees, projects, etc.
  • Perform/coordinate special projects for education within the Department or MGBfC as may arise from time-to-time.

Residency and Fellowship Program Responsibilities

  • Works collaboratively with Division Chiefs and Program Directors to support the programs.
  • Provides general administrative support to the program directors.
  • Serves as a resource for trainees and coordinators.
  • Oversees and participates in recruitment related activities including maintenance of the ERAS databases (ERAS) for multiple fellowship programs, coordinating in-person and/or virtual interviews, and ensure all required policies are shared with applicants.
  • Responds to inquiries from trainees and applicants and triages as necessary to others within the department or in other hospital/MGB departments.
  • Monitors credentialing and appointment related activities including licensure, malpractice, moonlighting, visas, etc. working collaboratively with the Department Credentialing Manager, the Medical Staff Office, and the MGB Office for Global Professionals and Scholars (GPS) or ECFMG.
  • Creates annual contracts for incoming and returning fellows across the clinical accredited fellowships, based on GME templates, policies, and procedures.
  • Develops the annual department orientation for incoming fellows across multiple programs, to include institutional aspects (IDs, Occ Health, security access, benefits, required annual talks); communicates with incoming fellows regarding parking, required on-line Healthstream and EPIC training, housing etc.; monitors completion of required trainings by incoming fellows; assists in the preparation of annual training materials.
  • Supports communication with trainees including informing trainees of inter and intradepartmental policy and procedure changes, with assistance from GME office.
  • Organizes fellowship information, and maintains program(s) brochures and Orientation and recruitment materials to ensure up-to-date information is available for applicants, new fellows, and transitioning fellows.
  • Prompts divisions to update web sites periodically with regard to education pages.
  • Organizes meetings, conferences, lectures, retreats, and other events including preparation and distribution of materials and attendance tracking.
  • Maintains essential program data and trainee files including records of fellows relating to evaluation and required bi-annual meetings with the program director.
  • Manages the evaluative processes of trainees, the program, the faculty and experiences or rotations.
  • Notifies pediatric staff and appropriate hospital offices of terminated fellows and forwarding information.
  • Manages materials for specialty-specific national, annual trainee exams, and may proctor exams.
  • Evaluates and standardizes programmatic procedures with subspecialty pediatric programs and in some cases core programs; makes recommendations for curricular and programmatic improvements to Program Directors.
  • Exercises independent judgment effectively troubleshoots and resolves issues as they arise to facilitate smooth and prompt responses to program changes.
  • Prepares for and assists in the readiness of the program for accreditation activities including data maintenance, collection and organization of materials, and team-preparation for ACGME Self Studies, ACGME Site Visits, GME Special Reviews, and GME Internal reviews.
  • May attend annual, specialty specific Association of Directors of Training national conferences and/or national meetings. May attend to national duties as regional representative (or other) to said Association.
  • May hold a position or present/attend regional and national conferences if elected/selected, such as National Society of Academic Medical Administrators (NSAMA) or ACGME annual conferences; May serve or present on GME-related committees.
  • Develops agenda for Education Leadership Committee in conjunction with Program Directors and department education leadership; may present materials or topics; records minutes.
  • Participates in process improvement efforts across education programs.
  • Learns new systems to support education programs as necessary.
  • Performs other duties and assists with projects as assigned by the Pediatric Vice Chair of Education, Program Directors, and MGBfC Administrative Director.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor's degree required. Master’s Degree preferred

Minimum of 5 years of office administration experience in a healthcare and/or education setting

Prior experience in administration of graduate medical education programs strongly preferred

TAGME certification

Notary preferred

SKILLS/ ABILITIES/ COMPETENCIES REQUIRED:

With the increasing scope and complexity of program requirements and documentation, the program manager must have excellent organizational skills, effective analytical skills and have an ability to exercise independent and sound judgment. Must be able to triage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a complex environment with multiple interruptions. Excellent communications skills are essential, including verbal, written, and computer communication abilities. Strong critical thinking, problem-solving and attentiveness to detail required. This individual will be interacting with a variety of staff at many levels, often dealing with confidential information and strong interpersonal skills are critical. Must possess excellent computer skills including MS Word, Excel, and Outlook. Experience with web authoring would be helpful. Knowledge of, or ability to learn other software programs, especially GME New Innovations, hospital specific software (i.e., Workday), and other database management programs as necessary (i.e. ERAS, WebADS). Knowledge of basic financial analysis and budget processes helpful.

Other Information

  • Works collaboratively with numerous staff supporting the subspecialty training programs
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to multi-task and organize information.
  • Ability to handle sensitive information with absolute confidentiality.
  • Working knowledge of software applications including Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  • Ability to make decisions independently or to escalate issues as needed.
  • Customer-service orientation.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Normal office conditions.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY:

Under direction of the program directors assists in oversight of educational administrative support staff; currently 4 direct reports.

FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY:

Manages education operating and capital budgets.


Additional Job Details (if applicable)

Schedule: Monday - Friday | 8am to 4:30pm | Onsite | 2 days Hybrid after 90 days of training; depending on department needs

Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 403b retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, discounted MBTA pass & more!

title: Principal Software Engineer - Multi-Cloud - Control Plane - Kubernetes
description:
Position Location:
This is a Flexible (Hybrid) position. Flexible positions require 2 days per week in a ServiceNow office. We have offices in several locations, including Santa Clara, CA, San Diego, CA, and Kirkland, WA

Cloud Platform — Kubernetes, Hyperscalers & Distributed Systems

We are currently seeking a Distinguished Engineer. In this role, you will have org-wide technical authority, giving you the ability to set technical direction across multiple engineering organizations. You will own the hardest, most ambiguous problems in the platform domain.

What you get to do in this role:

  • You will set the technical direction for our cloud-native platform across multiple engineering teams and organizations, defining the architecture and standards for how Kubernetes, distributed systems, and hyperscaler infrastructure are built and operated at scale.
  • You will own the hardest, most ambiguous technical problems in the platform domain — multi-cloud topology, control-plane design, workload isolation, identity and trust fabric, and reliability at the scale of hundreds of clusters and dozens of product workloads.
  • You will partner with engineering fellows, principal engineers, and other senior technical leaders to drive consistent architectural decisions and the adoption of best practices across the entire platform ecosystem.
  • You will identify and mitigate the biggest technical risks in initiatives with C-suite visibility, and you will be the person leadership trusts to make the call on managed vs. self-managed tradeoffs, substrate portability, and multi-hyperscaler strategy.
  • Where you see the need, you will personally design and build the critical components — control planes, operators, infrastructure abstractions, and the systems other teams build on top of.
  • You will mentor staff and principal engineers and shape the next generation of the organization’s technical leadership.

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Experience leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into engineering and platform work — whether using AI-powered tooling, automating operational workflows, building agentic systems for fleet visibility and operations, or reasoning about AI’s impact on how infrastructure is built and run.
  • 12+ years of experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems in production, with deep expertise running Kubernetes at scale (multi-cluster, multi-region, multi-tenant).
  • Hands-on, authoritative experience across one or more major hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP), including their managed Kubernetes offerings (EKS, AKS, GKE) and the networking, IAM, and capacity tradeoffs that come with each.
  • A proven track record of providing technical leadership across multiple engineering teams, influencing architecture and direction without relying on positional authority.
  • Deep expertise in the core building blocks of a modern platform: the operator/controller pattern, infrastructure-as-code and control planes (e.g., Crossplane), GitOps-based delivery, container networking (CNI), and service mesh.
  • Strong programming skills in Go and fluency across the cloud-native ecosystem.

It also helps if you have:

  • Experience designing identity and trust fabrics for distributed systems — workload identity, mTLS, and standards such as SPIFFE/SPIRE.
  • Experience with multi-tenant workload isolation and runtime security (e.g., Kata Containers, sandboxed runtimes).
  • Experience building and operating platforms for regulated or federal markets (FedRAMP, air-gapped or self-hosted distribution, OCI bundling).
  • Experience with observability at scale — metrics, tracing, and SLO-driven operations across a large fleet.
  • A platform-as-product mindset: treating internal engineering teams as customers and the platform as a product with a roadmap, contracts, and a delivery pipeline.

title: Java AWS Software Engineer III
description:
We have an opportunity to impact your career and provide an adventure where you can push the limits of what's possible.

As Software Engineer III at JPMorgan Chase within Commercial & Investment Bank - Post Trade Technology Reporting team, you are an integral part of an agile team that works to enhance, build, and deliver trusted market-leading technology products in a secure, stable, and scalable way. As a core technical contributor, you are responsible for conducting critical technology solutions across multiple technical areas within various business functions in support of the firm’s business objectives. This group is going through a migration and modernization journey where you will be contributing to designing products, owning the design end-to-end, designing & building applications, and testing activities.

Job responsibilities

  • Develop code that conforms to the design, addresses non-functional requirements, and complies with the coding standards and conventions

  • Create detailed Unit Test cases, perform unit testing, integration testing, support QA and User acceptance testing and also address ad hoc user queries

title: RN-TSS
description:
Behavioral Health Network (BHN) is a leading statewide provider of behavioral health services and a Certified Great Place to Work. Since 1938, BHN has helped individuals, families, and communities thrive through compassionate, high-quality care and support. With deep roots in Western Massachusetts and a growing presence in communities throughout the state, we are currently seeking a Registered Nurse to join our Transitional Support Services (TSS) team and help advance our mission of empowering people to live healthier, more fulfilling lives.

What We Offer:

  • Purpose-Driven Work – Make a meaningful impact in the lives of individuals, families, and communities throughout Western Massachusetts.
  • Professional Growth – Access ongoing training, mentorship, career development, and advancement opportunities across one of the region's largest behavioral health organizations.
  • Supportive Team Culture – Join a collaborative workplace guided by our HEART values: Humanity, Empowerment, Accountability, Respect, and Teamwork.
  • Stability & Opportunity – Build your career with a well-established organization serving Western Massachusetts since 1938.
  • Comprehensive Benefits – Generous PTO, 403(b), educational assistance, medical, dental, vision, employee assistance programs, and more.
  • Certified Great Place to Work – Work for an organization recognized for creating a positive and engaging employee experience.

What You Will Do:

  • Provide compassionate, person-centered clinical and nursing services to individuals receiving care through BHN's Transitional Support Services (TSS) program.
  • Complete comprehensive intake and ongoing nursing assessments, including review of systems, diagnoses, mental status, vital signs, recovery needs, and emerging medical or behavioral-health concerns.
  • Transcribe, verify, and administer medications as ordered; maintain accurate medication records; inventory medications; coordinate refills; and dispose of outdated or unused medications according to program policy.
  • Use nursing assessment and clinical judgment to identify health needs and implement appropriate treatment or referral responses that support safe recovery and continued stabilization.
  • Consult regularly with the Nurse Manager, providers, pharmacies, program staff, significant others, and community partners to coordinate treatment, address medical needs, and promote continuity of care.
  • Provide individuals, groups, families, and staff with education about recovery, health, wellness, medications, self-management skills, and strategies that support long-term progress.
  • Build rapport and trust with individuals served while maintaining a safe, healthy, respectful, and recovery-oriented milieu with appropriate professional boundaries.
  • Triage nursing workflow during assigned shifts, participate in treatment-planning and transition meetings, and respond effectively to changing or urgent clinical needs.
  • Complete nursing assessments, progress notes, medication orders, discharge summaries, and other required clinical documentation clearly, accurately, and on time.
  • Support aftercare planning and transitions to community-based services or the next appropriate level of care; maintain required licensure and continuing education; and perform other duties as assigned.

Who You Are:

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Current, unrestricted Massachusetts Registered Nurse license required.
  • At least one year of experience or training working in behavioral health and one year of post-graduate medical-surgical nursing experience required.
  • Basic understanding of behavioral-health conditions, recovery principles, co-occurring needs, and appropriate pharmaceutical, medical, and psychoeducational interventions required.
  • Ability to complete comprehensive nursing assessments, identify medical and psychiatric needs, administer medications safely, and coordinate appropriate treatment and referrals.
  • Ability to provide high-quality transitional and recovery-focused care and educate individuals about health, wellness, medications, self-management, and community supports.
  • Strong clinical judgment, critical thinking, problem-solving, adaptability, organization, time-management, and prioritization skills, including the ability to respond effectively to urgent needs.
  • Demonstrated cultural responsiveness and ability to establish rapport and work respectfully with individuals from diverse backgrounds and with complex needs.
  • Excellent interpersonal, teamwork, technology, and verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to maintain timely and accurate electronic documentation.
  • Ability to serve as essential staff and meet the physical requirements of the role, including regular standing, walking, and sitting and lifting or carrying up to 25 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

We Hire for HEART!

Since 1938, BHN has delivered high-quality, culturally responsive behavioral health care, building deep roots in Western Massachusetts while expanding our impact in communities throughout the state. Our core values—Humanity, Empowerment, Accountability, Respect, and Teamwork—guide how we lead, serve, and support one another. If you’re ready to bring your skills and experience to a mission-driven organization where your work can make a meaningful difference, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Platform Engineer - m/f/d
description:
Where Europe's enterprises adopt AI

Langdock is the AI platform used by more than 10,000 companies to give employees secure access to the leading AI models, to build and share agents and to automate repetitive workflows. We have grown past $40M ARR while remaining a small team, and we care deeply about operating efficiently across the entire company.

For many enterprises, Langdock is becoming the place where most of the net-new work is produced. As people and agents create more documents, analyses, decisions, and automations inside AI interfaces, the context and data behind that work accumulate within Langdock. This gives us the opportunity to earn a larger role in their technology stack by building a platform they choose to rely on.

Our ambition is to build that platform for European enterprises while preserving their control over data, model providers, and deployment environments. We have made meaningful progress at the application layer, but much of the foundation beneath it still needs to be built.

You can watch the Meet the engineering team video to get a feeling for how we work.

The role

Platform Engineers own the shared capabilities that Langdock's products are built on. They treat these capabilities as internal products: defining the interfaces other teams build against and remaining accountable for their reliability, evolution, and operation over time.

The work is to turn complex capabilities such as model access, agent execution, authorization, queues, integrations, document processing, and sandboxed compute into stable, reusable building blocks. Each capability needs a clear contract and must be able to evolve without forcing coordinated changes across the rest of the product.

You own a service from design through long-term operation. That includes defining its API and failure behavior, planning migrations, implementing and deploying it, making it observable, and responding when it fails in production. When a service requires a new underlying mechanism, you work with Systems Engineers while remaining accountable for the service boundary and lifecycle.

What you might work on

Current platform work includes:

  • A durable agent runtime. The current engine runs model and tool loops for Chat, Workflows, automations, and subagents, but active execution is still owned by one process. We are separating the runtime from product-specific state and designing durable runs that can wait for approvals or external events, recover after a process dies, and continue without repeating committed tool calls. This also includes deterministic context reconstruction, compaction, and prompt-cache efficiency.

  • The Model Gateway. We are building one inference boundary for every Langdock product, with a model-agnostic API over managed and customer-provided models. The work includes provider adapters, routing across accounts and regions, rate limits, bounded fallback, streaming safety, usage tracking, and a control plane.

  • Shared services with explicit contracts. We are moving selected capabilities out of a TypeScript monolith into independently operated services with Protobuf and gRPC contracts inside one Bazel monorepo. Our authorization service, written in Go with embedded SpiceDB, is one example: the migration uses an outbox, shadow comparisons on production traffic, and consistency tokens before it becomes authoritative.

  • The integration and tool platform. Langdock already connects to external services through REST APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication. The platform work is to make authentication, token refresh, rate limits, approvals, outbound network safety, and tool execution consistent across these paths.

  • Code execution as a shared service. Langdock already runs untrusted JavaScript, Bash, and Python through separate execution environments. Platform work includes defining a consistent execution API, lifecycle, permission model, resource budgets, and operational boundary, while partnering with Systems Engineers on the underlying isolation and scheduling mechanisms.

  • Production confidence for shared systems. Platform changes need evidence before rollout. Current work includes a reusable load-testing system for HTTP, gRPC, and streaming workloads; structured logging without user content or personally identifiable information (PII); and online database changes for PostgreSQL tables measured in hundreds of gigabytes or terabytes.

You will start in one area based on your experience and the team's priorities, then own its interface and operation in production.

Tech stack

  • TypeScript and a growing set of Go services in one Bazel monorepo

  • Next.js, React, and Tailwind on the front end

  • Node.js services and workers on the back end

  • PostgreSQL with Prisma; Redis with BullMQ

  • Protobuf and gRPC for service contracts

  • Kubernetes across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on-premises deployments

  • Terraform and Terragrunt for infrastructure orchestration

  • Datadog and Sentry for observability

You should be familiar with most of this. We trust you to pick up the rest quickly.

How we work

  • We operate with high trust and autonomy in squads of 3 to 4 engineers. A squad owns its roadmap, prioritization, technical decisions, and operation in production. Engineers are expected to find the context they need, ask for input when it improves the outcome, and move work forward without waiting for every next step to be assigned.

  • We align asynchronously before scheduling a meeting. Product requirement documents (PRDs) define the user problem, intended outcome, and constraints. Design documents make architectural boundaries, tradeoffs, failure modes, migrations, and rollouts explicit. People read and challenge the thinking asynchronously; once the context is shared, a short in-office discussion or whiteboard session usually resolves the remaining questions quickly.

  • We optimize for leverage. Engineers choose the AI tools that work for them, supported by clear ticket context, focused branches, automated tests, and AI review before human review. We also invest in observability, migration tooling, automated recovery, and runbooks so recurring product maintenance does not depend on someone remembering a manual step.

  • The engineer who ships a change owns it in production. If something breaks, you lead the fix.

What we are looking for

  • You have several years of experience, typically 3 to 6, building and operating backend systems under real load. You are strong in TypeScript and Node.js and comfortable with Kubernetes, Terraform, networking, databases, and queues. Experience with Go is useful; willingness to work in it matters more.

  • You have strong platform design judgment and approach foundational work with diligence. You can define stable service boundaries and APIs while accounting for data integrity, tenant isolation, backward compatibility, partial failure, and safe rollout.

  • Given an underspecified systems problem, you identify the most important invariant, decide where to go deep, and defend what you deliberately leave out. You investigate unfamiliar components and failure modes until you understand the underlying mechanism.

  • You treat deployment as the start of ownership. You make systems observable, respond when they fail, and turn incidents into lasting improvements while moving with calm urgency and maintaining a high standard.

  • You use AI tools to multiply your output while remaining responsible for the architecture and every change that ships. You share context, ask for input, disagree directly and respectfully, and help other engineers succeed.

Working here

This is an in-office role at Greifswalder Strasse 212 in Berlin. We work together in person because it helps us build trust, develop shared context, and make decisions quickly.

Most engineers start around 8:30. We usually eat lunch together, and dinner is available for people who stay later. Running and gym are part of the routine for many of us.

You need an existing right to work in Germany. We do not currently sponsor visas.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is €90,000–€140,000 gross per year. All roles include equity.

We will figure out the right level together based on your experience and scope. Levels are about the work you own, not your title or years of experience. Salaries are tied to levels, not negotiation.

The Production Scheduler is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing production schedules to ensure efficient use of manufacturing resources, timely order fulfillment, and alignment with customer demand. This role serves as the key link between Sales, Operations, and Procurement to balance capacity, materials, and labor planning. The position drives the execution of the production plan, monitors performance, and proactively resolves scheduling conflicts to maintain service levels and production efficiency.

This role will actively support company goals by improving scheduling accuracy, optimizing lead times, and enhancing communication across departments to achieve operational excellence.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of manufacturing process flow, capacity planning, and material requirements planning (MRP).
  • Familiarity with barcode scanning systems and production reporting tools.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.

title: Lead Compliance Engineer
description:
About Halter

At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund, Bessemer Venture Partners, BOND, DCVC, Blackbird, Promus Ventures, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram.

About the role

Halter's expansion is gated by market access. Every country we enter, every product we ship, and every cellular network we join passes through certification and right now we're entering markets faster than ever: NZ, Australia, USA, Canada, EU, UK, South America, and Africa. We're looking for a Lead Compliance Engineer to own this domain end-to-end: radio/wireless, EMC/EMI, product safety, and carrier certification for our collars, towers, and supporting hardware.

You'll report directly to the Head of Hardware, alongside our electronics and mechanical leaders, and be the single point of ownership for turning world-class engineering into products farmers can buy, and doing so at the pace. This is not a checkbox function. Compliance done well is a competitive weapon: it decides how fast Halter reaches new farmers, and you'll be the one holding it.

What your day could look like

  • Owning the device testing and certification strategy — what gets tested, where, when, and to which standards — across every current and target market, running certification in parallel with development so compliance is never the blocker.

  • Selecting and managing third-party test labs, certification bodies, and in-country regulatory consultants — owning scope, cost, schedule, and quality of what they deliver.

  • Driving carrier certification end-to-end for our cellular-connected products, from test device logistics through lab engagement to network approval.

  • Building Halter's pre-compliance capability — in-house test equipment and trusted lab partnerships — so design iterations happen in days, not lab-booking weeks, and formal certification is a confirmation, not a discovery.

  • Partnering with electronics, RF, firmware, and mechanical engineers during design so products pass first time, and driving root cause when they don't.

  • Maintaining the compliance framework: standards matrix, certification register, technical files, and declarations of conformity — audit-ready, always.

  • Monitoring regulatory change across our markets and translating it into clear product and business impact before it becomes a problem.

  • And finally, this is a start-up, so you'll also be rolling your sleeves up and helping with whatever is required.

Who we're looking for

  • 8+ years in regulatory compliance and certification for wireless/electronic products, with a proven record of taking hardware through certification in multiple international markets.

  • Deep working knowledge of radio (FCC, ISED, RED, RCM), EMC/EMI, and product safety standards — and how to navigate the regulatory bodies behind them.

  • Experience with carrier/operator certification (e.g. PTCRB, GCF, or direct carrier approval programs) for cellular devices is highly valued.

  • A track record of managing third-party labs and consultants as an extension of your own capability — commercially sharp, technically uncompromising.

  • Hands-on pre-compliance test experience: you know your way around a spectrum analyser and can design out a failure, not just report it.

  • Comfortable operating with full autonomy — you'll set the strategy, own the budget, and answer for the outcome.

  • A positive person who seeks ownership and is a self-motivated problem solver.

  • Interested and available to travel internationally to labs, regulators, and manufacturers (~10–20% of the year).

Join our team

Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!

Please also feel free to check out the careers page for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn & Instagram.

Why our team loves working at Halter:

  • Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.

  • Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.

  • You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our $1,000 personal growth fund.

  • This isn't easy, and we love that it's hard. Working at Halter will be the most rewarding and the most challenging work of your life. We move fast, take bold bets, and work hard to reshape an entire industry. As one team member put it: "Joining Halter is a bit like strapping yourself to a rocket ship, but it's an epic journey to be a part of!"

description:

Since 1938, BHN has helped individuals, families, and communities thrive through compassionate, high-quality care and support. With deep roots in Western Massachusetts and a growing presence in communities throughout the state, we are currently seeking a Registered Nurse to join our Program of Assertive Community Treatment (PACT) team and help advance our mission of empowering people to live healthier, more fulfilling lives.

What We Offer:

  • Purpose-Driven Work – Make a meaningful impact in the lives of individuals, families, and communities throughout Western Massachusetts.
  • Professional Growth – Access ongoing training, mentorship, career development, and advancement opportunities across one of the region's largest behavioral health organizations.
  • Supportive Team Culture – Join a collaborative workplace guided by our HEART values: Humanity, Empowerment, Accountability, Respect, and Teamwork.
  • Stability & Opportunity – Build your career with a well-established organization serving Western Massachusetts since 1938.
  • Comprehensive Benefits – Generous PTO, 403(b), educational assistance, medical, dental, vision, employee assistance programs, and more.
  • Certified Great Place to Work – Work for an organization recognized for creating a positive and engaging employee experience.

What You Will Do:

  • Provide direct and indirect nursing services to individuals served by BHN's Program of Assertive Community Treatment (PACT), collaborating with the multidisciplinary team to support coordinated, person-centered care.
  • Coordinate and complete assessments of individuals' physical-health needs, make appropriate referrals to community medical providers, and integrate medical and psychiatric treatment.
  • Follow Medication Administration Program (MAP) policies and procedures and complete health- and medication-related documentation in accordance with applicable requirements.
  • Under the direction of the team psychiatrist and in collaboration with PACT nurses, manage medications, pharmaceuticals, medical supplies, and related clinical workflows.
  • Support the development, implementation, review, and documentation of treatment plans, health goals, and recovery objectives, providing ongoing information about individuals' progress and needs.
  • Serve as primary case manager for an assigned caseload when requested, completing required assessments, treatment-plan reviews, and financial-management plans.

description:
Title of Position: Health and Safety Supervisor
Location: Percy Village

Gateways Hospital and Mental Health Center, located in Los Angeles, is a non-profit organization that provides an array of comprehensive mental health services for Children, Adolescents, Transitional Aged Youth, and Adults suffering from mental illness in the Greater Los Angeles area. The organization consists of a standalone fifty-five (55) )-bed hospital and six outlying outpatient facilities that have anywhere from fourteen (14) beds to one hundred and thirty-four (134) beds. The organization has approximately four hundred (400) employees.

SUMMARY OF POSITION

The Health and Safety Supervisor serves as the lead Paraprofessional Counselor during assigned shifts, providing guidance, training, and support to paraprofessional staff while ensuring the safe, secure, and effective operation of the residential facility. This position is responsible for monitoring the health, safety, and security of residents, staff, and property through routine rounds, hazard identification, security checks, and adherence to established protocols. The Health and Safety Supervisor responds to emergencies and crisis situations, promotes a therapeutic and recovery-oriented environment, and assists with daily program operations, including resident accountability, medication monitoring, meal service, documentation, and other paraprofessional counseling duties. The position serves as a resource to staff, supports operational continuity, and may act on behalf of the Residential Manager in their absence.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES

  • Maintains communication with team members throughout the shift to assure that all tasks are covered, and offers assistance where needed.
  • Monitors client sign in and out procedures and accountability procedures including: sign in /out cards, pass request forms, hourly rounds, AWOL procedures, etc.
  • Ensures that on duty or on call management is appropriately notified in emergency or other critical situations.
  • Receives and stocks supplies.
  • Conducts random security checks of premises and cottages as appropriate and/or assigned. Ensures life safety of all residents through proper observations and documentation of security rounds/checks.
  • Reports safety hazards, maintenance and housekeeping needs to the Residential Manager.
  • Observes and records resident behavior and activities, monitors hygiene. Reports any unusual or concerning behavior to the appropriate staff members.
  • Monitors and ensures that clients take prescribed psychotropic medications, and that medications are accurately recorded.
  • Monitors client living areas and works with clients to understand and maintain minimum health and safety standards in their assigned living space.
  • Responds appropriately to emergency or problematic situations; i.e. notifies immediate supervisor, staff, administration, police, fire department, ambulance and paramedics as appropriate.
  • Assists in situational crisis intervention as needed.
  • Provides a good role model for residents and paraprofessional staff in terms of reliability, social skills, professionalism, tact, leadership, grooming and integrity.
  • Assists in hazard monitoring and other data collection and reporting as needed to maintain facility safety standards.
  • In conjunction with Program Director, serves as acting supervisor when Residential Manager is off duty or on leave.
  • Assists with quality reports, scheduling, and professional interdepartmental communications with Facilities Management, Environmental Services, Dietary Services, Human Resources, Contracted Security Services, Substance Abuse Testing Agencies, or executive management.
  • Assists in scheduling coverage, or covering shifts as needed.
  • Performs additional tasks as assigned by Residential Manager or other members of the management team.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS

  • Knowledge of health, safety, security, and emergency response procedures in a residential or behavioral healthcare environment.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment and maintain professionalism during crisis and emergency situations.
  • Effective leadership, coaching, and conflict resolution skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to document observations, incidents, and resident activities accurately and timely.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and external service providers.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize multiple tasks and responsibilities.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries.
  • Basic computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office applications and electronic health record systems.

title: Research Assistant/Associate, Healthy Aging [LKCMedicine]
description:
The Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine (LKCMedicine) trains doctors who put patients at the centre of their exemplary care. The School, which offers both undergraduate and graduate programmes, is named after local philanthropist Tan Sri Dato Lee Kong Chian. Established in 2010 by Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, in partnership with Imperial College London, LKCMedicine aims to be a model for innovative medical education and a centre for transformative research. The School’s primary clinical partner is the National Healthcare Group, a leader in public healthcare recognised for the quality of its medical expertise, facilities and teaching. The School is transitioning to an NTU medical school ahead of the 2028 successful conclusion of the NTU-Imperial partnership to set up a Joint Medical School. In August 2024, we welcomed our first intake of the NTU MBBS programme, that has been recently enhanced to include themes like precision medicine and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare, with an expanded scope in the medical humanities. Graduates from the five-year undergraduate medical degree programme will have a strong understanding of the scientific basis of medicine, with an emphasis on technology, data science and the humanities.

We are looking for a highly motivated Research Assistant/Associate to join the LKCMedicine’s Centre for Geroscience and Geromedicine to focus on various aspects of translational bat immunology and aging research. The work will be conducted in a research group led by Nanyang Assistant Professor Matae Ahn who is a pioneer in bat immunology. The projects focus on learning from bats with exceptional healthy longevity to develop bat-inspired new targets and strategies to fight human diseases and aging, and have multiple national and international collaborations.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Conduct accurate monitoring, documenting and reporting of experimental results and/or research findings.

  • Maintain a safe, highly organized laboratory environment by managing equipment and consumables, while leading workplace safety and risk assessments.

  • Assist researchers in data analysis and literature review in various research projects.

  • Evaluate and interpret collected data and prepare oral presentations, written reports and scientific manuscripts for publication.

  • Perform other related duties incidental to the work described therein.

Key Competencies and Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree or Master’s degree in Life Sciences, Biotechnology, Bioengineering, Veterinary Science or related field.

  • Prior experience in the areas of immunology or aging is preferred but not compulsory for those with good academic and/or research track record.

  • Prior experience in animal work, tissue processing/histology, or single-cell & spatial transcriptomics library preparation is a major advantage. Candidates without prior exposure to these areas must demonstrate a strong learning agility and a proactive drive to master new workflows quickly.

  • Equipped with effective organizational and interpersonal communications with excellent written, oral communication and computer skills.

  • A team player who is able to prioritize, multi-task and work collaboratively in a diverse workforce.

We regret to inform that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

title: Business Solutions Technician
description:
Job Title: Business Solutions Technician

Wage: Starting at $28.50 per hour, DOE

Department: Business Services

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Reports To: Business Services Supervisor

Location: Willcox



Purpose of Position

The Business Solutions Technician is responsible for installing, maintaining, and planning local networks, routers, firewalls, servers, Wi-Fi, PCs, and other network equipment for managed IT service clients. This role also supports business development efforts by assisting the Business Sales Specialist with customer needs assessments, technical planning, solution design, and job details needed to develop accurate customer quotes. The role provides technical support, ensures network security, optimizes performance, collaborates closely with clients to understand their needs, and implements effective solutions. Strong problem-solving skills, customer service skills, and the ability to communicate technical information clearly are essential for success in this position.


Duties and Responsibilities

  • Actively encourages teamwork, open communication, and cooperative interaction by promoting a positive work environment that reflects the company’s mission, values and management
  • Works with the Business Sales Specialist and Business Services staff to identify customer needs and recommend appropriate managed IT, voice, data, network, and security solutions.
  • Conducts site visits, technical assessments, and discovery conversations to gather requirements for new installations, upgrades, and job planning.
  • Develops technical plans, network layouts, equipment recommendations, and scopes of work that align with customer needs and company standards.
  • Provides technical job details, equipment requirements, labor considerations, and installation information to the Business Sales Specialist for quote development.
  • Explains complex technical concepts in clear, customer-friendly language and assists with product or service demonstrations as needed.
  • Coordinates with internal technical, operations, and customer service teams to ensure proposed solutions can be implemented effectively and supported after installation.
  • Provides professional technical support and exceptional customer service to customers and end users.
  • Installs, configures, maintains, and troubleshoots managed IT systems and network infrastructure, including computers, servers, software, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless access points, and related equipment.
  • Installs, terminates, labels, tests, and documents structured cabling and fiber optic infrastructure, including network drops, patch panels, equipment racks, cable management systems, and telecommunications equipment.
  • Reads, interprets, creates, and maintains technical documentation, wiring diagrams, and network records to support accurate installations, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
  • Diagnoses and resolves hardware, software, network, Wi-Fi, and connectivity issues while maintaining accurate documentation and escalating complex problems as needed.
  • Performs routine system maintenance, software updates, equipment testing, and preventative maintenance to ensure reliable system performance.
  • Accurately documents work performed, labor hours, materials used, equipment installed, configuration changes, test results, and service activities in accordance with company procedures.
  • Maintains the confidentiality and security of customer and company information while following company policies and industry best practices.
  • Follows all company safety policies, OSHA regulations, and job site requirements, including the proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE), and safely operates ladders, lifts, bucket trucks, and other equipment when trained and authorized.
  • Maintains a clean, organized, and professional work environment at customer locations, company facilities, vehicles, and job sites.
  • Demonstrates flexibility by adapting to changing customer needs, technologies, work environments, and departmental priorities.

Qualifications

  • Computer Experience: Basic personal computer skills including electronic mail, word processing, routine database, spreadsheet, graphics, and related business applications. Experience with managed IT services, networking equipment, firewalls, Wi-Fi systems, hosted voice or telecommunications services, job planning tools, and customer relationship management systems is desirable. Experience and understanding of the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model Layers 1-3 is highly desirable but not essential.
  • Planning/Organization: Ability to prioritize, handle multiple tasks and organize assignments simultaneously.
  • Language Skills: Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, procedure manuals, technical specifications, customer requirements, scopes of work, and service agreements. Ability to write routine reports, correspondence, job planning notes, and technical support information for customer solutions. Ability to communicate effectively with customers, employees, sales staff, vendors, and management, including the ability to explain technical information in clear, customer-friendly terms. Bi-lingual in English and Spanish is desirable.
  • Mathematical Skills: Ability to add and subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rates, ratios, and percents and to draw and interpret graphs.
  • Reasoning Ability: Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagram form. Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations.


Certificates/Licenses

    Under 1/3rd of the time.

Regularly exposed to outside weather conditions and/or indoor shop environment with adequate ventilation. May be required to climb ladders and carry equipment up to 50 pounds. Your Role

The ERP Functional Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Lead will lead the analysis, design, implementation, and support of JD Edwards EnterpriseOne (E1) Supply Chain modules. This role is critical in optimizing supply chain operations, improving efficiencies therein, and ensuring ERP system alignment with business goals. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in ERP systems, particularly JD Edwards, and will be responsible for driving system enhancements, troubleshooting, and providing functional support for supply chain processes supported by the JD Edwards systems at Vantive. The Integrated Supply Chain Lead will also collaborate closely with third-party support and delivery teams to ensure effective and efficient solutions are implemented to streamline manufacturing operations.


Vantive is a recent divestiture of a larger company. The candidate will play a key role in cloning the current applications to stand up a new technology landscape which allows Vantive to operate separately from the previous owner’s systems and exit from the Transition Services Agreements (TSA). This is an exciting opportunity to join a newly formed company and make a difference in the healthcare industry.


What You’ll be Doing

  • Fulfilling the JD Edwards Integrated Supply Chain SME role, supporting Sales Order Management, Procurement, Advanced Warehousing, Inventory Management, Quality Management, Transportation Management, EDI, and Inventory Management modules within JD Edwards EnterpriseOne system.
  • Working with the Business Relationship Manager (BRM) and technology teams to ensure business needs are clearly understood and JD Edwards Supply Chain solutions meet the needs and expectations of the business.
  • Ensure that the JDE Supply Chain and Distribution modules are aligned with medical device industry compliance standards, including FDA regulations. Support validation documentation, traceability, electronic records/signatures, audit readiness, and robust change control procedures to meet regulatory and quality system requirements.
  • Actively participate in the program to clone JD Edwards applications and processes into Vantive’s JDE instances and ensure the cloned applications are working as expected.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Technology, Finance, Manufacturing, Commercial, HR, etc) to ensure smooth integration of the JDE Supply Chain processes with the business processes supported by these teams.
  • Work closely with business stakeholders to understand requirements and translate them into functional specifications and system solutions.
  • Partner with third-party support and delivery teams to manage and resolve any issues related to JD Edwards applications, ensuring timely and effective delivery of system enhancements and support.
  • Configure and support JD Supply Chain modules, ensuring business needs are met and processes are streamlined.
  • Preferred: Experience with Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), such as Swisslog, including integration with JD Edwards EnterpriseOne. Understanding of automated warehouse operations, inventory control, material handling systems, and real-time data exchange to support efficient distribution workflows.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve integration errors with WMS and other supply chain systems interfaced with Vantive’s JDE instances.
  • Provide end-user training, documentation, and ongoing support to ensure effective system adoption.
  • Drive and lead JD Edwards EnterpriseOne upgrade initiatives, contributing deep functional expertise across manufacturing modules. Oversee requirements definition, impact assessments, functional validation, and user enablement to ensure smooth transition and optimal system performance after the upgrade.
  • Play a critical role in continuous improvement initiatives by utilizing cloned applications to develop more efficient, scalable, and adaptable solutions.

title: Growth & Partnerships Lead
description:
About Us

At Cast & Crew, we’ve empowered creativity and supported the global entertainment industry for decades. Together with our family of brands - Backstage, CAPS, Checks & Balances, Final Draft, Media Services, Sargent-Disc, and The TEAM Companies – we operate as a combined entertainment technology and services provider offering industry standard screenwriting accounting software, digital payroll products, data & reporting, and a host of creative tools. The industry continues to move faster than ever, and the need for our expertise, our technology, and our people has never been greater. We are a production’s best ally every step of the way. #OneCastOneCrew

Final Draft has been the industry standard in screenwriting software for over 30 years. Ninety-five percent of Hollywood productions are written on it. Studios expect it. Film programs teach it. Writers depend on it. The brand does not need an introduction.

What it needs is a growth system. Final Draft has never had a dedicated outbound motion. The white space is real, the relationships are warm, and the product sells itself once the right conversation starts. This role exists to start more of them.

Position Overview

We are looking for someone who can look at a brand with this much recognition, ask where it isn't, and then go there. You will build campaigns, run nurture programs, develop partnerships, identify new market opportunities, and own the motion from first contact to qualified conversation. You will also own For Your Consideration outreach to studios during awards season, a high-visibility initiative that puts Final Draft directly in front of decision-makers at the moment they are most engaged.

There is a strong foundation here. An experienced account manager owns the existing revenue base. The HubSpot infrastructure exists. The customer relationships are real and deep. Your job is to build the system that finds new revenue and generates it more deliberately than we ever have.

Core Responsibilities

Outbound & Campaign Engine

  • Design and execute outbound campaigns across studio, production company, new and education segments using Jeeva, HubSpot, and LinkedIn

  • Build sequences and continually test and improve based on results

  • Run nurture programs for lapsed accounts, closed-lost prospects, and dormant contacts already in the database

  • Monitor Variety, Deadline, and industry news for new productions and emerging companies, and turn that intelligence into outreach

  • Own abandoned cart and inbound inquiry pipelines for new enterprise prospects and own the process to turn them into customers

White Space & Market Expansion

  • Pilot new segments in controlled campaigns before scaling, so we know what works before we commit to it

  • Own the white space analysis that feeds Jeeva targeting, paid ads strategy, and outbound sequencing

Partnerships & Industry Presence

  • Own For Your Consideration ad sales to studios during awards season, coordinating timing, messaging, and follow-through

  • Identify sponsorship and partnership opportunities across industry events, screenwriting community events, and adjacent tools in the production ecosystem

  • Create and plan industry tradeshow representation opportunities for Final Draft at UFVA, PGA, and other industry events in an effort to obtain new business leads

Content & Sales Assets

  • Build sales assets, pitch materials for EDU and new buyers, email workflow assets that slot directly into Jeeva sequences. Assets include case studies, white papers, and other downloadable content to help in the sales process.

  • Audit competitor product pages and surface improvements to the Final Draft enterprise experience in partnership with marketing

Campaign Operations & Reporting

  • Own Jeeva as a growth tool — build workflows, manage sequences, monitor performance, and keep the CRM clean and useful

  • Deliver on weekly activity KPIs including SQLs, Prospecting Emails Sent, Open Rate, New Deals, Meetings Booked, and Closed Deals

  • Partner with Marketing leadership on paid ads strategy, providing the ICP, messaging, and success metrics needed to run campaigns that reinforce the outbound motion

  • Track performance relentlessly and make decisions based on data

title: UAV Tech - L3
description:
Summary

The UAV Technician II serves as a key member of the manufacturing and testing team, building on the assembly and lower level technical skills with advanced troubleshooting, system expertise, and leadership responsibilities. This position is the first line of escalation for diagnosing and resolving complex technical issues with both UAV products and testing systems. The UAV Technician II acts as a critical liaison between assembly/technician teams and engineering, providing detailed feedback, technical expertise, and recommendations to ensure streamlined operations, product quality, and ongoing process improvements.

The ideal candidate will possess a deep understanding of the UAV systems and processes, including avionics, mechanical components, software, and testing tools, while demonstrating problem-solving proficiency, excellent communication skills, and leadership qualities to assist and mentor other team members.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other Duties not listed may be assigned.

  • Assembly and Integration Operations:
    • Perform and oversee advanced hands-on assembly of UAV systems, including avionics, airframes, propulsion and communications systems, sensors, and payloads, following detailed SOPs and technical documentation.
    • Execute and ensure completion of advanced integration tasks, including firmware installation and system configuration/setup.
    • Assist and mentor junior team members in all aspects of UAV assembly and integration.
  • Troubleshooting, Testing, and Quality Assurance:
    • Lead the troubleshooting of escalated technical issues with UAV sub-assemblies, flight control systems, and fully assembled aircraft.
    • Diagnose and resolve complex problems across electrical, mechanical, and software systems using tools such as multimeters, oscilloscopes, diagnostic software, and testing rigs.
    • Oversee functional testing of UAVs, sub-assemblies, and test systems to verify performance, reliability, and compliance with specifications.
    • Perform calibration, validate system performance, and document outcomes during debugging and testing phases.
  • Escalation Point for Complex Issues:
    • Serve as the first escalation point for assembly or testing issues that require greater technical depth or a multidisciplinary approach.
    • Analyze, document, and clearly communicate detailed failure modes, observations, and potential solutions to engineers for product refinement or issue resolution.
    • Assist engineers with root cause analysis, system audits, and test plan execution when diagnosing recurring or systemic issues.
  • Communication and Liaison Role
    • Act as the direct go-between for assembly/technician teams and engineering, ensuring a seamless flow of technical information and feedback.
    • Document and communicate findings from testing and troubleshooting to assist engineering teams with product design updates, system enhancements, or technical documentation improvements.
    • Provide feedback to production and engineering teams to improve assembly processes, SOPs, and test systems, balancing quality with production efficiency..
  • Mentorship and Leadership
    • Assist in the training and mentoring of UAV Assemblers and Technician I team members, helping them develop greater technical knowledge and troubleshooting skills.
    • Verify and approve work completed by junior team members, ensuring quality and adherence to SOPs and company standards.
    • Foster a collaborative team environment by proactively addressing questions, sharing knowledge, and supporting team growth.
  • Continuous Improvement and Safety Compliance
    • Identify and implement opportunities for improving production, testing, and troubleshooting workflows to enhance efficiency, quality, and safety.
    • Ensure all work performed complies with the company’s safety, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.
    • Assist in the upkeep of testing systems and equipment, ensuring functionality, calibration, and reliability.

This role is located on-site and there is no option for remote work. This is a rotating 24x7 shift work on 365-day work schedule.

Position Overview:

The GMD SITR program is a critical part of our nation’s layered Ballistic Missile Defense System providing the U.S. with the capability to engage and intercept long range ballistic missiles during midcourse flight.

Essential Functions:

  • Support the 24x7 operations of the GMD Fire Control (GFC) and GMD Communications Network (GCN) component of the GMD system.

  • Use SolarWinds and other network management tools to monitor, detect and report faults to hardware devices, virtual machines, and network connections.
